explanation: High availability requires redundancy—horizontal scaling provides this naturally. Multiple servers mean one failure doesn't cause outage. Vertical scaling creates single point of failure; even reliable hardware eventually fails.

question: Rukmini, whom Krsna carried away, was the daughter of which king?

options.B: King Bhismaka

explanation: "Attracted by the beauty and fortune of Rukmini, the daughter of King Bhismaka, many great princes and kings assembled to marry her." (SB 3.3.3)

subtopic: Ch 3: The Lord's Pastimes Out of Vrndavana
question: By subduing seven bulls whose noses were not pierced, whose hand did the Lord achieve?

options.B: Satyabhama

explanation: "By subduing seven bulls whose noses were not pierced, the Lord achieved the hand of Princess Nagnijiti in the open competition to select her bridegroom." (SB 3.3.4)

subtopic: Ch 3: The Lord's Pastimes Out of Vrndavana
question: Just to please His dear wife, what did the Lord bring back from heaven, just as an ordinary husband would do?

options.B: The parijata tree

explanation: "Just to please His dear wife, the Lord brought back the parijata tree from heaven, just as an ordinary husband would do." (SB 3.3.5)

subtopic: Ch 3: The Lord's Pastimes Out of Vrndavana
question: Narakasura, killed by the Lord, was the son of whom?

options.B: Dharitri, the earth

explanation: "Narakasura, the son of Dharitri, the earth, tried to grasp the whole sky, and for this he was killed by the Lord in a fight." (SB 3.3.6)

subtopic: Ch 3: The Lord's Pastimes Out of Vrndavana
question: What did the princesses kidnapped by Narakasura offer when they saw the Lord, the friend of the distressed?

options.B: To be His wives

explanation: "They looked upon Him with eagerness, joy and shyness and offered to be His wives." (SB 3.3.7)

subtopic: Ch 3: The Lord's Pastimes Out of Vrndavana
question: How many offspring did the Lord beget in each and every one of His wives?

options.B: Five

explanation: "The Lord begot in each and every one of them ten offspring with exactly His own qualities." (SB 3.3.9)

subtopic: Ch 3: The Lord's Pastimes Out of Vrndavana
question: When Kalayavana, the King of Magadha and Salva attacked Mathura, why did the Lord refrain from killing them personally?

options.B: Just to show the power of His own men

explanation: "The Lord refrained from killing them personally, just to show the power of His own men." (SB 3.3.10)

subtopic: Ch 3: The Lord's Pastimes Out of Vrndavana
question: Of the demons Sambara, Dvivida, Bana, Mura, Balvala and Dantavakra, how did the Lord deal with them?

options.B: He caused all to be killed by others
options.C: Some He killed Himself, and some He caused to be killed by others
options.D: He banished them from the kingdom

explanation: "Some He killed Himself, and some He caused to be killed by others [Sri Baladeva, etc.]." (SB 3.3.11)

subtopic: Ch 3: The Lord's Pastimes Out of Vrndavana
question: What was the great burden of the earth, eighteen aksauhinis, abated with the help of Drona, Bhisma, Arjuna and Bhima?

options.B: The Battle of Kuruksetra

explanation: "The abatement of the earth's great burden, eighteen aksauhinis, has now been effected with the help of Drona, Bhisma, Arjuna and Bhima." (SB 3.3.14)

subtopic: Ch 3: The Lord's Pastimes Out of Vrndavana
question: According to the Lord, how would the great strength of the Yadu dynasty finally disappear?

options.A: By a great war with the demigods
options.B: When they quarrel among themselves, influenced by intoxication

explanation: "When they quarrel among themselves, influenced by intoxication, with their eyes red like copper because of drinking [madhu], then only will they disappear." (SB 3.3.15)

subtopic: Ch 3: The Lord's Pastimes Out of Vrndavana
question: Whom did Lord Krsna establish in the position of supreme control of the world to show the ideal of administration on the path of piety?

options.B: Maharaja Yudhisthira

explanation: "Lord Sri Krsna... established Maharaja Yudhisthira in the position of supreme control of the world in order to show the ideal of administration on the path of piety." (SB 3.3.16)

subtopic: Ch 3: The Lord's Pastimes Out of Vrndavana
question: The embryo begotten by Abhimanyu in the womb of Uttara was burnt by whose weapon, but later protected by the Lord?

options.B: Karna

explanation: "The embryo of Puru's descendant begotten by the great hero Abhimanyu in the womb of Uttara, his wife, was burnt by the weapon of the son of Drona, but later he was again protected by the Lord." (SB 3.3.17)

subtopic: Ch 3: The Lord's Pastimes Out of Vrndavana
question: How many horse sacrifices did the Supreme Lord induce the son of Dharma (Yudhisthira) to perform?

options.B: Two

explanation: "The Supreme Lord induced the son of Dharma to perform three horse sacrifices." (SB 3.3.18)

subtopic: Ch 3: The Lord's Pastimes Out of Vrndavana
question: In conformity with which system of philosophy was the Lord situated in detachment and knowledge while enjoying life in Dvaraka?

options.B: The Sankhya system

explanation: "He was situated in detachment and knowledge, as enunciated by the Sankhya system of philosophy." (SB 3.3.19)

subtopic: Ch 3: The Lord's Pastimes Out of Vrndavana
question: After many years of household life in Dvaraka, what was at last fully manifested in the Lord?

options.B: His detachment from ephemeral sex life
options.C: His wish to rule the world

explanation: "The Lord was thus engaged in household life for many, many years, but at last His detachment from ephemeral sex life was fully manifested." (SB 3.3.22)

subtopic: Ch 3: The Lord's Pastimes Out of Vrndavana
question: Who can put faith in Lord Krsna's transcendental sense activities?

options.B: One who has become a devotee of the Lord by rendering devotional service

explanation: "No one, therefore, can put his faith in Lord Krsna's transcendental sense activities but one who has become a devotee of the Lord by rendering devotional service." (SB 3.3.23)

subtopic: Ch 3: The Lord's Pastimes Out of Vrndavana
question: Why did the great sages curse the princely descendants of the Yadu and Bhoja dynasties?

options.A: Because they were made angry by the sporting activities of the princes, as desired by the Lord
options.B: Because the princes refused them charity

explanation: "Great sages were made angry by the sporting activities of the princely descendants of the Yadu and Bhoja dynasties, and thus, as desired by the Lord, the sages cursed them." (SB 3.3.24)

subtopic: Ch 3: The Lord's Pastimes Out of Vrndavana
question: When the descendants of Vrsni, Bhoja and Andhaka went to Prabhasa, who remained in Dvaraka?

options.B: Those who were eternal devotees of the Lord

explanation: "Those who were eternal devotees of the Lord did not leave but remained in Dvaraka." (SB 3.3.25)

subtopic: Ch 3: The Lord's Pastimes Out of Vrndavana
question: The Lord learned all Vedas simply by hearing them once from __________.

options.B: His father Vasudeva

subtopic: Ch 3: The Lord's Pastimes Out of Vrndavana
question: Rukmini, whom the Lord carried away to marry was the daughter of King __________.

options.B: Bhismaka

subtopic: Ch 3: The Lord's Pastimes Out of Vrndavana
question: By subduing 7 bulls, the Lord achieved the hand of Princess __________.

options.B: Satyabhama

subtopic: Ch 3: The Lord's Pastimes Out of Vrndavana
question: __________ was the son of Dharitri, who had held 16000 princesses as captives.

options.B: Madhu

subtopic: Ch 3: The Lord's Pastimes Out of Vrndavana
question: Lord begot in each and every wife ________ sons.

subtopic: Ch 3: The Lord's Pastimes Out of Vrndavana
question: Maharaja Yudhistira performed ______ horse sacrifices induced by Krishna.
After partaking of the remnants of prasada, what liquor did the descendants of Vrsni and Bhoja drink, making them delirious?

options.B: Liquor made of rice

explanation: "All of them... partook of the remnants of prasada and also drank liquor made of rice." (SB 3.4.1)

question: At what time of day did the interaction of the faults of intoxication cause their minds to become unbalanced and destruction to take place?

options.B: At noon

explanation: "At sunset, by the interaction of the faults of intoxication, all their minds became unbalanced, and destruction took place." (SB 3.4.2)

question: After foreseeing the end of His family, where did Lord Krsna go to sip water and sit down underneath a tree?

options.B: The bank of the river Sarasvati

explanation: "The Personality of Godhead, Lord Sri Krsna, after foreseeing the end [of His family] by His internal potency, went to the bank of the river Sarasvati, sipped water, and sat down underneath a tree." (SB 3.4.3)

question: Where had the Lord previously told Uddhava to go?

options.B: Badarikasrama

explanation: "Thus He who desired to destroy His family told me previously to go to Badarikasrama." (SB 3.4.4)

question: Why did Uddhava follow Krsna even though he knew of the Lord's desire to destroy the dynasty?

options.B: Because it was impossible for him to bear separation from the lotus feet of the master
options.C: Because he wanted to witness the destruction
options.D: Because he was afraid to be alone

explanation: "I followed Him because it was impossible for me to bear separation from the lotus feet of the master." (SB 3.4.5)

question: By which features did Uddhava immediately recognize the Lord as the Supreme Personality of Godhead?

options.B: His four hands, different symbolic representations, and yellow silk garments

explanation: "I could immediately recognize Him as the Supreme Personality of Godhead by His four hands, different symbolic representations, and yellow silk garments." (SB 3.4.7)

question: Against what kind of tree was the Lord sitting and taking rest in His final pastime?

options.B: A mango tree

explanation: "The Lord was sitting, taking rest against a young banyan tree, with His right lotus foot on His left thigh." (SB 3.4.8)

question: What did the Lord tell Uddhava (Vasu) about the association Uddhava had desired in days of yore?

options.A: That it was impossible to obtain
options.B: That it is very difficult for others to obtain, but He awards it unto him
options.C: That Uddhava must earn it through penance
options.D: That only Brahma could grant it

explanation: "You particularly desired to achieve My association. This is very difficult for others to obtain, but I award it unto you." (SB 3.4.11)

question: To which transcendental abode did the Lord tell Uddhava he could now go by leaving this universe?

options.B: Vaikuntha

explanation: "Now you can go to My transcendental abode, Vaikuntha, by leaving this universe of conditioned living entities." (SB 3.4.12)

question: To whom did the Lord say He had spoken His transcendental glories, described by sages as Srimad-Bhagavatam, at the beginning of creation?

options.B: Brahma, situated on the lotus from His navel

explanation: "I spoke unto Brahma, who is situated on the lotus that grows out of My navel, about My transcendental glories, which the great sages describe as Srimad-Bhagavatam." (SB 3.4.13)

question: Among the four principles of religiosity, economic development, sense gratification and liberation, what did Uddhava prefer to engage in only?

options.B: The loving service of the Lord's lotus feet

explanation: "I have preferred only to engage in the loving service of Your lotus feet." (SB 3.4.15)

question: What knowledge did Uddhava request the Lord to explain, which the Lord had explained before to Brahmaji?

options.B: Transcendental knowledge which gives enlightenment about the Lord

explanation: "Kindly explain to us... that transcendental knowledge which gives enlightenment about Yourself and which You explained before to Brahmaji." (SB 3.4.18)

question: Where did Uddhava say he was proceeding for association, as instructed by the Lord?

options.B: Badarikasrama in the Himalayas

explanation: "I am now proceeding to Badarikasrama in the Himalayas for association, as I have been instructed by Him." (SB 3.4.21)

question: In which incarnation has the Personality of Godhead been undergoing great penance at Badarikasrama since time immemorial?

options.B: As the sages Nara and Narayana

explanation: "The Personality of Godhead, in His incarnation as the sages Nara and Narayana, has been undergoing great penance since time immemorial for the welfare of all amiable living entities." (SB 3.4.22)

question: From whom did Uddhava advise Vidura to take lessons for the reception of transcendental knowledge?

options.B: The great learned sage Maitreya

explanation: "You may take lessons from the great learned sage Maitreya, who is nearby and who is worshipable for reception of transcendental knowledge." (SB 3.4.26)

question: On the bank of which river did Uddhava pass the night with Vidura as if it were a moment, before going away?

options.B: The Ganges

explanation: "After thus discussing with Vidura the transcendental name, fame, qualities, etc., on the bank of the Yamuna, Uddhava was overwhelmed with great affliction." (SB 3.4.27)

question: According to Sukadeva Gosvami, the cursing of the brahmanas was only a plea, but what was the actual fact?

options.B: The supreme desire of the Lord

explanation: "The cursing of the brahmanas was only a plea, but the actual fact was the supreme desire of the Lord." (SB 3.4.29)

question: Why could Uddhava remain in this world to disseminate knowledge of the Personality of Godhead?

options.A: Because he was the eldest devotee
options.B: Because he is never affected by the modes of material nature
options.C: Because he was a great scholar

explanation: "Uddhava is not inferior to Me in any way because he is never affected by the modes of material nature." (SB 3.4.31)

question: Upon understanding that he was remembered by Lord Krsna while quitting this world, what did Vidura do?

options.B: He began to cry loudly, overwhelmed by the ecstasy of love

explanation: "Understanding that he was remembered by Lord Krsna... Vidura began to cry loudly, overwhelmed by the ecstasy of love." (SB 3.4.35)

question: After passing a few days on the bank of the Yamuna, on the bank of which river did Vidura reach where the great sage Maitreya was situated?

options.B: The Ganges

explanation: "After passing a few days on the bank of the river Yamuna, Vidura, the self-realized soul, reached the bank of the Ganges, where the great sage Maitreya was situated." (SB 3.4.36)

question: The Lord asked Uddhava to go to _____ to spend the rest of his days.

options.B: JagannathPuri

question: In His last lila, the Lord was sitting and resting against a young _____ tree.

options.B: Banyan

question: During His ending lila, while the Lord spoke with Uddhava, _____ approached that place.

options.B: Vidhura

question: Uddhava desired only to _____.

options.A: Engage in the loving service of the Lord's lotus feet
options.B: Always remember the Lord
options.C: Serve the Lord from his mind, body and soul

question: The Lord resides in Badarikashrama in His incarnation as _____.

options.B: Vamanadeva

question: Vidura was instructed by Uddhava to receive transcendental knowledge from _____.

options.B: NaraNarayana Rsi

question: At the opening of the chapter, why was Satī moving in and out of the room "as a swing moves this way and that"?

options.A: She was preparing decorations to welcome her father to Lord Śiva's home
options.B: Her mind was divided between the desire to see her relatives and her fear of Lord Śiva's warning
options.C: She was searching the house for her pet bird before the journey
options.D: She was performing a yogic exercise to steady her breathing

explanation: "The sage Maitreya said: Lord Śiva was silent after speaking to Satī, seeing her between decisions. Satī was very much anxious to see her relatives at her father's house, but at the same time she was afraid of Lord Śiva's warning. Her mind unsettled, she moved in and out of the room as a swing moves this way and that." (Purport: "Satī's mind was divided about whether to go to her father's house or obey the orders of Lord Śiva. The struggle between the two decisions was so strong that she was pushed from one side of the room to another, and she began to move just like the pendulum of a clock.")

question: According to the purport, what was the Vedic conception of the family relationship that existed between Lord Śiva and Satī when it is said he "had given her half his body"?

options.A: The husband owns the wife's body completely
options.B: The husband gives half his body to his wife, and the wife gives half of her body to her husband, so that a husband without a wife or a wife without a husband is incomplete
options.C: The wife must give her entire body to her husband while he retains his own
options.D: Half the body is given only at the time of death

explanation: "According to the Vedic conception of family life, the husband gives half his body to his wife, and the wife gives half of her body to her husband. In other words, a husband without a wife or a wife without a husband is incomplete."

question: The word 'apratipūruṣam' is used to describe Lord Śiva when Satī looked at him "as if she were going to blast him with her vision." What does the purport say this word means and indicate?

options.A: "One who is easily angered," indicating Śiva's temper
options.B: "One who has no equal" / "the personality who has no rival"; since Śiva is the ātmā, it indicates Satī was prepared to commit suicide
options.C: "One who lives in the crematorium," indicating his inauspicious dwelling
options.D: "One who cannot be seen," indicating Śiva's invisibility

explanation: "The word apratipūruṣam, used in this verse, means 'one who has no equal.' ... In other words, since Lord Śiva is the ātmā (śiva also means ātmā), it is indicated here that Satī was prepared to commit suicide. Another meaning of the word apratipūruṣa is 'the personality who has no rival.'"

question: In the purport describing Satī leaving her husband, what does the text identify as the general cause of separation and divorce between husband and wife?

options.B: Interference from in-laws
options.D: The husband's neglect of religious duties

explanation: "Generally, separation between husband and wife is due to womanly behavior; divorce takes place due to womanly weakness. The best course for a woman is to abide by the orders of her husband. That makes family life very peaceful."

question: Which of Lord Śiva's disciples are named as those who, headed the thousands of followers, quickly followed Satī when she left alone?

options.B: Maṇimān and Mada

explanation: "When they saw Satī leaving alone very rapidly, thousands of Lord Śiva's disciples, headed by Maṇimān and Mada, quickly followed her with his bull Nandi in front and accompanied by the Yakṣas."

question: The word 'anucarāḥ' used to describe Lord Śiva's disciples following Satī is explained to mean what?

options.A: "Those who are afraid of their master"
options.B: "Those who ride upon bulls"
options.C: "Those who can immediately understand the purpose of their master"

explanation: "The word anucarāḥ is also significant, for it indicates that Lord Śiva's disciples were always ready to sacrifice anything for Lord Śiva. All of them could understand the desire of Śiva, who did not want Satī to go alone. Anucarāḥ means 'those who can immediately understand the purpose of their master.'"

question: How did Lord Śiva's disciples arrange for Satī to travel to her father's house?

options.A: On foot, surrounded by an armed guard
options.B: In a golden chariot pulled by horses
options.C: Seated on the back of a bull, given her pet bird, a lotus flower, a mirror, and covered with a great canopy, in a pompous procession
options.D: Carried in a palanquin by the Yakṣas alone

explanation: "The disciples of Lord Śiva arranged for Satī to be seated on the back of a bull and gave her the bird which was her pet. They bore a lotus flower, a mirror and all such paraphernalia for her enjoyment and covered her with a great canopy. Followed by a singing party with drums, conchshells and bugles, the entire procession was as pompous as a royal parade."

question: Regarding the animals gathered at the sacrifice, what does the purport clarify was their real purpose?

options.A: They were meant to be killed and eaten as prasādam
options.B: They were kept as pets for the demigods
options.C: They were used to test the power of Vedic mantras — an old animal was offered in the fire and rejuvenated to test the brāhmaṇas' realization, not to be killed for meat
options.D: They were traded as payment to the priests

explanation: "That these animals were meant for sacrifice does not mean that they were meant to be killed. ... to test their realization an old animal was offered in the fire and rejuvenated. That was the test of a Vedic mantra. The animals gathered were not meant to be killed and eaten. The real purpose of a sacrifice was not to replace a slaughterhouse but to test a Vedic mantra by giving an animal new life. Animals were used to test the power of Vedic mantras, not for meat."

question: When Satī arrived at the sacrificial arena, who welcomed her, and why did no one else?

options.A: Her father welcomed her; the others were busy chanting
options.B: Only her mother and sisters welcomed her with tears; the others were afraid of Dakṣa
options.C: The demigods welcomed her; her family ignored her
options.D: The brāhmaṇas welcomed her; her mother was absent

explanation: "When Satī, with her followers, reached the arena, because all the people assembled were afraid of Dakṣa, none of them received her well. No one welcomed her but her mother and sisters, who, with tears in their eyes and with glad faces, welcomed her and talked with her very pleasingly."

question: Although her mother and sisters offered her greetings, a seat, and presents, why did Satī refuse to accept anything?

options.B: Because Lord Śiva had forbidden her from accepting gifts
options.C: Because her father neither talked with her nor welcomed her by asking about her welfare
options.D: Because she was fasting for the sacrifice

explanation: "Although she was received by her sisters and mother, she did not reply to their words of reception, and although she was offered a seat and presents, she did not accept anything, for her father neither talked with her nor welcomed her by asking about her welfare."

question: What position did Satī hold among Dakṣa's children, and how had that relationship changed?

options.A: She was the eldest and remained Dakṣa's favorite
options.B: She was the youngest child and had been his pet, but because of her association with Lord Śiva, Dakṣa forgot all his affection for her
options.C: She was a middle child whom Dakṣa never favored
options.D: She was adopted and thus never truly loved

explanation: "Satī was the youngest child of Dakṣa, and she knew that she was his pet. But now, because of her association with Lord Śiva, Dakṣa forgot all his affection for his daughter, and this very much aggrieved her."

question: What specific observation at the sacrifice made Satī 'greatly angry, so much so that she looked at her father as if she were going to burn him with her eyes'?

options.A: That her sisters had been given better seats than her
options.B: That there were no oblations for her husband Lord Śiva, and that Dakṣa had neither invited Śiva nor received her
options.C: That the brāhmaṇas were arguing instead of chanting
options.D: That the sacrificial animals were being mistreated

explanation: "Present in the arena of sacrifice, Satī saw that there were no oblations for her husband, Lord Śiva. Next she realized that not only had her father failed to invite Lord Śiva, but when he saw Lord Śiva's exalted wife, Dakṣa did not receive her either. Thus she became greatly angry, so much so that she looked at her father as if she were going to burn him with her eyes."

question: The purport states that when Viṣṇu or a Vaiṣṇava is insulted, one should be angry, and cites Lord Caitanya as an example. On whose behalf did Lord Caitanya become angry and want to kill the offenders?

options.A: When Advaita was offended by the demigods
options.B: When Nityānanda was offended by Jagāi and Mādhāi
options.C: When Haridāsa Ṭhākura was beaten in the marketplace
options.D: When His own mother was insulted

explanation: "Lord Caitanya, who always preached nonviolence, meekness and humility, also became angry when Nityānanda was offended by Jagāi and Mādhāi, and He wanted to kill them. When Viṣṇu or a Vaiṣṇava is blasphemed or dishonored, one should be very angry."

question: In her speech, how does Satī characterize Lord Śiva's attitude toward all living entities to prove that only Dakṣa could be envious of him?

options.A: Śiva loves only his devotees and hates the demons
options.B: Śiva is the most beloved of all living entities, has no rival, no one is very dear to him and no one is his enemy, being free from all enmity
options.C: Śiva favors the demigods above ordinary men
options.D: Śiva is indifferent and cares for no one

explanation: "The blessed goddess said: Lord Śiva is the most beloved of all living entities. He has no rival. No one is very dear to him, and no one is his enemy. No one but you could be envious of such a universal being, who is free from all enmity."

question: Satī addresses Dakṣa as 'dvija' (twice-born) and contrasts his fault-finding with a great soul's vision, using the analogy of what creature that seeks only honey?

options.B: A bee, which is always interested in the honey in the flower and does not consider the thorns and colors
options.C: A swan separating milk from water
options.D: An ant collecting only sweet grains

explanation: "Just as a bee is always interested in the honey in the flower and does not consider the thorns and colors, highly qualified persons, who are uncommon, accept only the good qualities of others, not considering their bad qualities, whereas the common man can judge what are good qualities and what are bad qualities."

question: In the purport to Text 12, the story of a devotee who wanted the benediction that 'whenever he touched someone on the head, that person's head would at once be separated from his trunk' is used to illustrate which name and quality of Lord Śiva?

options.B: Āśutoṣa — one who is satisfied very easily and offers the highest benediction, magnifying even a small good quality
options.D: Vṛṣadhvaja — one who carries the bull banner

explanation: "Lord Śiva is also called Āśutoṣa, which refers to one who is satisfied very easily and who offers to any person the highest level of benediction. For example, once a devotee of Lord Śiva wanted the benediction that whenever he touched someone on the head, that person's head would at once be separated from his trunk. Lord Śiva agreed. ... Thus Lord Śiva accepted his bad qualities as magnificently good qualities."

question: Satī says the name of Lord Śiva, 'consisting of two syllables, śi and va,' does what? And what does 'śiva' mean according to the purport?

options.B: It purifies one of all sinful activities; śiva means maṅgala, or auspicious
options.C: It brings victory in battle; śiva means 'conqueror'
options.D: It ensures long life; śiva means 'eternal'

explanation: "Satī continued: My dear father, you are committing the greatest offense by envying Lord Śiva, whose very name, consisting of two syllables, śi and va, purifies one of all sinful activities. ... Śiva means maṅgala, or auspicious. Within the body the soul is auspicious."

question: The purport uses the analogy of milk and curd (from the Brahma-saṁhitā) to explain the position of Lord Śiva relative to the Supreme Personality of Godhead. What is the point of this analogy?

options.A: Lord Śiva and Lord Viṣṇu are exactly equal, like two cups of the same milk
options.B: Lord Śiva is like curd — in one sense he is the Supreme Personality of Godhead, but in another sense he is not, just as curd is milk yet we must distinguish between the two
options.C: Lord Śiva is superior to Viṣṇu, as curd is thicker than milk
options.D: Lord Śiva has no relation to Viṣṇu, as water differs from milk

explanation: "Lord Śiva is described in the Brahma-saṁhitā to be like curd or yogurt. Curd is not different from milk. Since milk is transformed into curd, in one sense curd is also milk. Similarly, Lord Śiva is in one sense the Supreme Personality of Godhead, but in another sense he is not, just as curd is milk although we have to distinguish between the two."

question: Satī prescribes what one should do upon hearing an irresponsible person blaspheme the master and controller of religion. What is the graded instruction she gives?

options.A: One should always forgive the blasphemer and continue chanting
options.B: If unable to punish, block one's ears and go away; but if able, one should by force cut out the blasphemer's tongue and kill the offender, and after that give up one's own life
options.C: One should report the blasphemer to the king for judgment
options.D: One should debate the blasphemer until he is convinced

explanation: "Satī continued: If one hears an irresponsible person blaspheme the master and controller of religion, one should block his ears and go away if unable to punish him. But if one is able to kill, then one should by force cut out the blasphemer's tongue and kill the offender, and after that one should give up his own life."

question: According to the purport of Text 17, the response to hearing blasphemy differs by social order. Why did Satī decide to give up her own body rather than kill Dakṣa?

options.A: Because she was physically unable to harm him
options.B: Because she considered herself among the vaiśyas and śūdras (with whom women are grouped), who should immediately give up their bodies upon hearing blasphemy of an exalted person
options.C: Because Lord Śiva had ordered her not to harm anyone
options.D: Because killing was forbidden inside a sacrificial arena

explanation: "But as far as the vaiśyas and śūdras are concerned, they should immediately give up their bodies. Satī decided to give up her body because she thought herself to be among the śūdras and vaiśyas. As stated in Bhagavad-gītā (9.32), striyo vaiśyās tathā śūdrāḥ. Women, laborers and the mercantile class are on the same level."

question: Satī compares her rejection of the body received from Dakṣa to what medical analogy?

options.B: Vomiting — 'If someone has taken food which is poisonous, the best treatment is to vomit'

explanation: "Therefore I shall no longer bear this unworthy body, which has been received from you, who have blasphemed Lord Śiva. If someone has taken food which is poisonous, the best treatment is to vomit."

question: According to the purport of Text 18, why did Satī — described as the representation of the external potency of the Lord, able to vanquish many universes — choose to give up her own body instead of destroying Dakṣa?

options.A: Because she feared retaliation from the demigods
options.B: To save her husband from the charge that he employed his wife to kill Dakṣa because he could not do so himself due to his inferior position
options.C: Because she had lost her powers upon entering the arena
options.D: Because the Vedas forbid a woman from killing her father

explanation: "Since Satī was the representation of the external potency of the Lord, it was in her power to vanquish many universes, including many Dakṣas, but in order to save her husband from the charge that he employed his wife, Satī, to kill Dakṣa because he could not do so due to his inferior position, she decided to give up her body."

question: Satī explains that when Lord Śiva addresses her by a particular name during relaxed conversation, she becomes morose and her smile disappears. What is that name and its meaning?

options.B: Dākṣāyaṇī — 'the daughter of King Dakṣa'

explanation: "Because of our family relationship, when Lord Śiva addresses me as Dākṣāyaṇī I at once become morose, and my jolliness and my smile at once disappear. ... The word dākṣāyaṇī means 'the daughter of King Dakṣa.' Sometimes, when there was relaxed conversation between husband and wife, Lord Śiva used to call Satī 'the daughter of King Dakṣa,' and because this very word reminded her about her family relationship with King Dakṣa, she at once became ashamed."

question: After finishing her speech to Dakṣa, what did Satī do to prepare to give up her body?

options.A: She threw herself into the sacrificial fire pit
options.B: She sat down on the ground facing north, dressed in saffron/yellow garments, sanctified herself with water, closed her eyes, and absorbed herself in the mystic yoga process
options.C: She ran back toward Lord Śiva's abode
options.D: She drank poison offered at the altar

explanation: "Maitreya the sage told Vidura: O annihilator of enemies, while thus speaking to her father in the arena of sacrifice, Satī sat down on the ground and faced north. Dressed in saffron garments, she sanctified herself with water and closed her eyes to absorb herself in the process of mystic yoga."

question: Describe the yogic path by which Satī raised her life air before quitting her body.

options.A: From the head down to the feet
options.B: She placed the prāṇa and apāna in equilibrium near the navel, then raised the life air (mixed with intelligence) to the heart, then to the pulmonary passage, and from there to between the eyebrows
options.C: She circulated the air only within the heart
options.D: She held her breath entirely until the body stopped

explanation: "First of all she sat in the required sitting posture, and then she carried the life air upwards and placed it in the position of equilibrium near the navel. Then she raised her life air, mixed with intelligence, to the heart and then gradually towards the pulmonary passage, and from there to between her eyebrows."

question: By meditating on what did Satī become 'completely cleansed of all taints of sin' and quit her body in a blazing fire?

options.A: The sacrificial fire of her father
options.B: The holy lotus feet of her husband, Lord Śiva, the supreme spiritual master of all the world
options.D: The mantra of the Yajur Veda

explanation: "Satī concentrated all her meditation on the holy lotus feet of her husband, Lord Śiva, who is the supreme spiritual master of all the world. Thus she became completely cleansed of all taints of sin and quit her body in a blazing fire by meditation on the fiery elements."

question: According to the commentators cited in the purport of Text 27 (Śrī Jīva Gosvāmī and Śrī Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura), what happened to Satī when she 'quit her body'?

options.A: She attained a spiritual body and went to Vaikuṇṭha
options.B: She gave up her relationship with Dakṣa within her heart; being the superintendent deity of the external potency, she did not get a spiritual body but transferred to another (better) body — later taking birth as Pārvatī, daughter of the Himālayas
options.C: She merged into the Supreme and ceased to exist
options.D: She was reborn as a demigod on a higher planet

explanation: "According to Śrī Jīva Gosvāmī, that Satī quit her body means that she gave up within her heart her relationship with Dakṣa. Śrī Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura also comments that since Satī is the superintendent deity of the external potency, when she quit her body she did not get a spiritual body but simply transferred from the body she had received from Dakṣa. Other commentators also say that she immediately transferred herself into the womb of Menakā, her future mother." (Also, purport to Text 26: "in her next life she would take birth as the daughter of the Himālayas, Pārvatī, and then she would again accept Lord Śiva as her husband.")

question: Who is named as Satī's future mother, into whose womb she was said to have immediately transferred herself?

options.B: Menakā

explanation: "Other commentators also say that she immediately transferred herself into the womb of Menakā, her future mother. She gave up the body she had received from Dakṣa and immediately transferred herself to another, better body, but this does not mean that she got a spiritual body."

question: What happened in the universe at the moment Satī annihilated her body in anger?

options.A: The sun went dark and the earth trembled silently
options.B: There was a tumultuous roar all over the universe, with the demigods of different planets crying out 'hā hā' in astonishment
options.C: A rain of flowers fell from the heavens
options.D: The sacrificial fire was immediately extinguished

explanation: "When Satī annihilated her body in anger, there was a tumultuous roar all over the universe. Why had Satī, the wife of the most respectable demigod, Lord Śiva, quit her body in such a manner? ... There was a tumultuous roaring all over the universe in the societies of the demigods of different planets because Satī was the daughter of Dakṣa, the greatest of all kings, and the wife of Lord Śiva, the greatest of all demigods."

question: The purport to Text 28 draws a lesson from Satī's dissatisfaction despite her exalted material position. What is that philosophical point (citing SB 1.2.6)?

options.B: Even the greatest material opulence cannot give complete satisfaction; the ātmā becomes fully satisfied only by developing devotional service to the Absolute Truth (Adhokṣaja)
options.C: Only renunciation of all activity brings peace
options.D: Satisfaction comes from family relationships alone

explanation: "One cannot attain complete satisfaction even if one is situated in the greatest material opulence. ... Therefore Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (1.2.6) explains that one has to achieve real satisfaction (yayātmā suprasīdati), but ātmā — the body, mind and soul — all become completely satisfied only if one develops devotional service to the Absolute Truth (sa vai puṁsāṁ paro dharmo yato bhaktir adhokṣaje). Adhokṣaja means the Absolute Truth."

question: When the attendants of Lord Śiva rose up with uplifted weapons to kill Dakṣa, who stopped them, and by what means?

options.A: Lord Brahmā stopped them by his personal presence
options.B: Bhṛgu Muni offered oblations into the southern side of the sacrificial fire and uttered mantric hymns from the Yajur Veda by which the destroyers of yajña could be killed
options.C: Nandi the bull blocked their path
options.D: The demigods surrounded and disarmed them

explanation: "They came forward forcibly, but Bhṛgu Muni saw the danger and, offering oblations into the southern side of the sacrificial fire, immediately uttered mantric hymns from the Yajur Veda by which the destroyers of yajñic performances could be killed immediately."

question: What was the outcome when Bhṛgu Muni offered oblations into the fire, and how were Satī's attendants (the Pramathas and Guhyakas) driven off?

options.A: Lord Viṣṇu appeared and pacified everyone
options.B: Many thousands of demigods named Ṛbhus became manifested, empowered by Soma the moon, and they attacked the ghosts and Guhyakas with half-burned firebrands, causing them to flee — accomplished through brahma-tejas, brahminical power
options.C: A great flood extinguished the sacrifice and scattered the crowd
options.D: Dakṣa's soldiers defeated the attendants in battle

explanation: "When Bhṛgu Muni offered oblations in the fire, immediately many thousands of demigods named Ṛbhus became manifested. All of them were powerful, having achieved strength from Soma, the moon." And: "When the Ṛbhu demigods attacked the ghosts and Guhyakas with half-burned fuel from the yajña fire, all these attendants of Satī fled in different directions and disappeared. This was possible simply because of brahma-tejas, brahminical power."

question: At the source of which celestial river (Hardwar) did Vidura reach Maitreya, the fathomless learned sage?

options.B: The Ganges

explanation: "Vidura... thus reached the source of the celestial Ganges river [Hardwar], where Maitreya, the great, fathomless learned sage of the world, was seated." (SB 3.5.1)

question: What did Vidura observe that people gain from engaging in fruitive activities to attain happiness?

options.B: Neither satiation nor mitigation of distress; on the contrary they are only aggravated

explanation: "Everyone in this world engages in fruitive activities to attain happiness, but one finds neither satiation nor the mitigation of distress." (SB 3.5.2)

question: What did Vidura request Maitreya to narrate about how the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Lord of the three worlds, acts?

options.B: How He accepts incarnations and creates the cosmic manifestation with perfectly arranged regulative principles

explanation: "Kindly narrate how the Supreme Personality of Godhead... accepts incarnations and creates the cosmic manifestation with perfectly arranged regulative principles for its maintenance." (SB 3.5.5)

question: Although Vidura had heard about the higher and lower statuses of human society from Vyasadeva, with what was he NOT satisfied?

options.A: The nectar of topics about Krsna
options.B: The performance of sacrifices

explanation: "They have not satisfied me with the nectar of topics about Krsna." (SB 3.5.10)

question: According to Vidura, topics of the Lord can cut off one's bondage to family affection simply by what means?

options.B: By entering the holes of one's ears

explanation: "Such topics can cut off one's bondage to family affection simply by entering the holes of one's ears." (SB 3.5.11)

question: In which great work had Vyasa already described the transcendental qualities of the Lord?

options.B: The Mahabharata

explanation: "Your friend the great sage Krsna-dvaipayana Vyasa has already described the transcendental qualities of the Lord in his great work the Mahabharata." (SB 3.5.12)

question: Vidura lamented that people's duration of life is spoiled by eternal time while they involve themselves in what?

options.A: Philosophical speculation, theoretical ultimate goals of life, and different modes of ritual
options.B: Fighting and warfare

explanation: "I see how their duration of life is spoiled by eternal time while they involve themselves in presentations of philosophical speculation, theoretical ultimate goals of life, and different modes of ritual." (SB 3.5.14)

question: To what did Vidura compare Maitreya's describing the essence of all topics, the topics of the Lord?

options.B: A river flowing to the sea
options.C: The sun rising in the morning
options.D: A bird returning to its nest

explanation: "Just as bees collect honey from flowers, kindly describe the essence of all topics — the topics of the Lord." (SB 3.5.15)

question: Maitreya said it was not wonderful that Vidura accepted the Lord without deviation of thought, because Vidura was born from the semen of whom?

options.B: Vyasadeva

explanation: "It is not at all wonderful that you have so accepted the Lord without deviation of thought, for you were born from the semen of Vyasadeva." (SB 3.5.19)

question: Due to the cursing of which muni was Vidura born, when formerly he was King Yamaraja?

options.B: Manduvya Muni

explanation: "I know that you are now Vidura due to the cursing of Manduvya Muni and that formerly you were King Yamaraja, the great controller of living entities after their death." (SB 3.5.20)

question: Prior to the creation, how did the Personality of Godhead exist?

options.B: As one without a second

explanation: "The Personality of Godhead, the master of all living entities, existed prior to the creation as one without a second." (SB 3.5.23)

question: By what name is the external energy, through whose agency the entire material manifestation is made possible, known?

options.B: Maya or illusion

explanation: "This external energy is known as maya or illusion, and through her agency only is the entire material manifestation made possible." (SB 3.5.25)

question: When the transcendental purusa incarnation impregnates the material nature of three modes, what appears by the influence of eternal time?

options.B: The living entities

explanation: "The Supreme Living Being in His feature as the transcendental purusa incarnation... impregnates the material nature of three modes, and thus by the influence of eternal time the living entities appear." (SB 3.5.26)

question: What is the great causal truth, the mahat-tattva, transformed into, which is manifested in three phases of cause, effect and the doer?

options.B: False ego

explanation: "Mahat-tattva, or the great causal truth, transforms into false ego, which is manifested in three phases — cause, effect and the doer." (SB 3.5.29)

question: The false ego is transformed into mind by interaction with which mode?

options.B: The mode of passion

explanation: "The false ego is transformed into mind by interaction with the mode of goodness." (SB 3.5.30)

question: The sky is a product of what, which is the transformation of egoistic ignorance?

options.B: Form

explanation: "The sky is a product of sound, and sound is the transformation of egoistic ignorance." (SB 3.5.32)

question: Earth, the final physical element, is qualified primarily by which quality?

options.B: Touch

explanation: "Thus it was transformed into the earth, which is qualified primarily by smell." (SB 3.5.36)

question: Why are the controlling deities of the physical elements, though empowered expansions of Lord Visnu, described as offering fascinating prayers to the Lord?

options.B: Because they were entrusted with different functions of universal duties and were unable to perform them

explanation: "Because they were entrusted with different functions of universal duties and were unable to perform them, they offered fascinating prayers to the Lord as follows." (SB 3.5.38)

question: In their prayer, to what did the demigods compare the Lord's lotus feet that protect the surrendered souls?

options.B: A boat

explanation: "Your lotus feet are like an umbrella for the surrendered souls, protecting them from all the miseries of material existence." (SB 3.5.39)

question: In the final verse, what did the demigods, created from the mahat-tattva, request of the Supreme Self?

options.B: Perfect knowledge and potency to render Him service in subsequent creation

explanation: "Kindly award us Your perfect knowledge and potency so that we can render You service in the different departments of subsequent creation." (SB 3.5.51)

question: Vidura met Maitreya Rsi at the banks of which river?

options.B: Yamuna

question: What did Vidura inquire from Maitreya Rsi about?

options.A: The transcendental devotional service of the Lord
options.B: How Lord accepts incarnations and creates cosmic manifestation all perfectly
options.C: The auspicious characteristics of the Lord in His different incarnations

question: Vidura is pained to see how common people's duration is spoiled by what?

options.B: Theoretical ultimate goals of life

question: Vidura was formerly which King?

options.B: Viswaksena

question: What transforms into false ego, manifested in 3 phases?

options.B: Absolute truth

question: The false ego transforms into mind by interaction with which mode?

options.B: Passion

question: The sky is the product of what?

options.B: Water

subtopic: Ch 6: Creation of the Universal Form
question: Why had the progressive creative functions of the universe been suspended, as the Lord heard?

options.A: Due to the curse of a sage
options.B: Due to the noncombination of His potencies, such as the mahat-tattva
options.C: Due to a great devastating flood
options.D: Due to the absence of Brahma

explanation: "The Lord thus heard about the suspension of the progressive creative functions of the universe due to the noncombination of His potencies, such as the mahat-tattva." (SB 3.6.1)

subtopic: Ch 6: Creation of the Universal Form
question: Into how many elements did the Supreme Lord simultaneously enter, along with the goddess Kali, His external energy?

options.B: Twenty-three

explanation: "The Supreme Powerful Lord then simultaneously entered into the twenty-three elements with the goddess Kali, His external energy, who alone amalgamates all the different elements." (SB 3.6.2)

subtopic: Ch 6: Creation of the Universal Form
question: When the twenty-three principal elements were set in action by the will of the Supreme, what came into existence?

options.B: The gigantic universal form, or the visva-rupa body of the Lord

explanation: "When the twenty-three principal elements were set in action by the will of the Supreme, the gigantic universal form, or the visvarupa body of the Lord, came into existence." (SB 3.6.4)

subtopic: Ch 6: Creation of the Universal Form
question: The gigantic virat-purusa, known as Hiranmaya, lived for how long on the water of the universe?

options.B: One thousand celestial years
options.C: A thousand cycles of four yugas

explanation: "The gigantic virat-purusa, known as Hiranmaya, lived for one thousand celestial years on the water of the universe, and all the living entities lay with Him." (SB 3.6.6)

subtopic: Ch 6: Creation of the Universal Form
question: The gigantic universal form of the Supreme Lord is described as the first incarnation and plenary portion of whom?

options.B: Brahma

explanation: "The gigantic universal form of the Supreme Lord is the first incarnation and plenary portion of the Supersoul." (SB 3.6.8)

subtopic: Ch 6: Creation of the Universal Form
question: From which part of the gigantic form did Agni, or heat, separate?

options.B: His eyes

explanation: "Agni, or heat, separated from His mouth, and all the directors of material affairs entered into it in their respective positions." (SB 3.6.12)

subtopic: Ch 6: Creation of the Universal Form
question: Which deity entered the two nostrils of the gigantic form, enabling living entities to smell?

options.B: The dual Asvini-kumaras

explanation: "When the Lord's two nostrils separately manifested themselves, the dual Asvini-kumaras entered them in their proper positions..." (SB 3.6.14)

subtopic: Ch 6: Creation of the Universal Form
question: When the eyes of the gigantic form manifested, who entered them with the partial representation of eyesight?

options.B: Indra
options.C: The sun, the director of light

explanation: "The sun, the director of light, entered them with the partial representation of eyesight, and thus the living entities can have vision of forms." (SB 3.6.15)

subtopic: Ch 6: Creation of the Universal Form
question: When the genitals of the gigantic form manifested, who entered into them with his partial semen?

options.B: Mitra

explanation: "...then Prajapati, the original living creature, entered into them with his partial semen, and thus the living entities can enjoy sex pleasure." (SB 3.6.19)

subtopic: Ch 6: Creation of the Universal Form
question: Which deity entered the hands of the gigantic form, enabling the living entity to transact business for his livelihood?

options.B: Mitra
options.C: Indra, the ruler of the heavenly planets

explanation: "...Indra, the ruler of the heavenly planets, entered into them, and thus the living entity is able to transact business for his livelihood." (SB 3.6.21)

subtopic: Ch 6: Creation of the Universal Form
question: When the intelligence of the gigantic form manifested, who entered into it with the partial power of understanding?

options.A: Brahma, the lord of the Vedas
options.B: The moon demigod

explanation: "...Brahma, the lord of the Vedas, entered into it with the partial power of understanding, and thus an object of understanding is experienced by the living entities." (SB 3.6.23)

subtopic: Ch 6: Creation of the Universal Form
question: Who entered the materialistic ego of the gigantic form as the controller of false ego?

options.B: Rudra

explanation: "...into it entered Rudra, the controller of false ego, with his own partial activities, by which the living entity transacts his objective actions." (SB 3.6.25)

subtopic: Ch 6: Creation of the Universal Form
question: From which part of the gigantic form were the heavenly planets manifested?

options.B: From His abdomen

explanation: "...from the head of the gigantic form, the heavenly planets were manifested, and from His legs the earthly planets and from His abdomen the sky separately manifested themselves." (SB 3.6.27)

subtopic: Ch 6: Creation of the Universal Form
question: The demigods, who reside in the heavenly planets, are qualified by which mode?

options.B: The mode of ignorance
options.C: The superexcellent quality of the mode of goodness
options.D: A mixture of all three modes

explanation: "The demigods, qualified by the superexcellent quality of the mode of goodness, are situated in the heavenly planets..." (SB 3.6.28)

subtopic: Ch 6: Creation of the Universal Form
question: From which part of the virat form did the brahmanas, the natural teachers of society, come into existence?

options.B: From the mouth

explanation: "...the Vedic wisdom became manifested from the mouth of the virat, the gigantic form. Those who are inclined to this Vedic knowledge are called brahmanas..." (SB 3.6.30)

subtopic: Ch 6: Creation of the Universal Form
question: From which part of the gigantic virat form was the power of protection generated, in relation to which the ksatriyas came into existence?

options.B: The arms

explanation: "...the power of protection was generated from the arms of the gigantic virat form, and in relation to such power the ksatriyas also came into existence..." (SB 3.6.31)

subtopic: Ch 6: Creation of the Universal Form
question: The means of livelihood of the vaisyas, the production of grains and their distribution, was generated from which part of the Lord's form?

options.B: The mouth

explanation: "The means of livelihood of all persons, namely production of grains and their distribution to the prajas, was generated from the thighs of the Lord's gigantic form." (SB 3.6.32)

subtopic: Ch 6: Creation of the Universal Form
question: The sudras, who satisfy the Lord by service, are situated on which part of the Personality of Godhead?

options.B: The thighs

explanation: "Situated on the legs are the sudras, who satisfy the Lord by service." (SB 3.6.33)

subtopic: Ch 6: Creation of the Universal Form
question: After mature meditation for one thousand celestial years, what could Brahma, the original poet, know about the Supreme Soul?

options.B: That the glories of the Supreme Soul are inconceivable

explanation: "...the original poet, Brahma, after mature meditation for one thousand celestial years, could know only that the glories of the Supreme Soul are inconceivable." (SB 3.6.38)

subtopic: Ch 6: Creation of the Universal Form
question: According to the last verse, what failed to achieve success in knowing the Supreme Personality of Godhead?

options.A: Words, mind and ego, with their respective controlling demigods
options.B: Only the material senses
options.D: The demigods in the heavenly planets

explanation: "Words, mind and ego, with their respective controlling demigods, have failed to achieve success in knowing the Supreme Personality of Godhead." (SB 3.6.40)

question: Who expressed a pleasing request by asking a question while Maitreya was speaking?

options.B: Vidura, the learned son of Dvaipayana Vyasa

explanation: "...Vidura, the learned son of Dvaipayana Vyasa, expressed a request in a pleasing manner by asking this question." (SB 3.7.1)

question: Why is there no possibility of desire prompting the Lord to play, as boys are prompted to play?

options.A: Because He is busy with creation
options.B: Because He is self-satisfied and detached from everything at all times
options.D: Because He does not exist materially

explanation: "But there is no possibility of such desire for the Lord because He is self-satisfied and detached from everything at all times." (SB 3.7.3)

question: By what has the Lord caused the creation, maintenance and dissolution of this universe again and again?

options.A: By His self-sheltered potency of the three modes of material nature
options.B: By the demigods

explanation: "By His self-sheltered potency of the three modes of material nature, the Lord has caused the creation of this universe." (SB 3.7.4)

question: Vidura asked: the pure soul is pure consciousness and is never out of consciousness due to circumstances, time, situations or dreams. How then does he become engaged in what?

options.B: Nescience

explanation: "The pure soul is pure consciousness and is never out of consciousness, either due to circumstances, time, situations, dreams or other causes. How then does he become engaged in nescience?" (SB 3.7.5)

question: Vidura asked: with the Lord as Supersoul situated in every living being's heart, why do the living entities' activities result in what?

options.B: Misfortune and misery

explanation: "The Lord, as the Supersoul, is situated in every living being's heart. Why then do the living entities' activities result in misfortune and misery?" (SB 3.7.6)

question: How did Maitreya appear when he was first agitated by the inquisitive Vidura, before replying without hesitation?

options.B: Astonished

explanation: "...Maitreya, being thus agitated by the inquisitive Vidura, at first seemed astonished, but then he replied to him without hesitation, since he was fully God conscious." (SB 3.7.8)

question: Maitreya said the living entity is in distress regarding his self-identity, having no factual background, like a man who dreams what?

options.B: That he sees his head cut off

explanation: "The living entity is in distress regarding his self-identity. He has no factual background, like a man who dreams that he sees his head cut off." (SB 3.7.10)

question: Maitreya compared the self associated with matter to which reflected object that appears to tremble due to the water?

options.B: The moon reflected on water

explanation: "As the moon reflected on water appears to the seer to tremble due to being associated with the quality of the water, so the self associated with matter appears to be qualified as matter." (SB 3.7.11)

question: By whose mercy, through the process of devotional service in the mode of detachment, can the misconception of self-identity be gradually diminished?

options.B: The Personality of Godhead, Vasudeva

explanation: "But that misconception of self-identity can be diminished gradually by the mercy of the Personality of Godhead, Vasudeva, through the process of devotional service to the Lord in the mode of detachment." (SB 3.7.12)

question: Simply by chanting and hearing of the transcendental name and form of which Personality of Godhead can one achieve the cessation of unlimited miserable conditions?

options.B: Lord Brahma

explanation: "Simply by chanting and hearing of the transcendental name, form, etc., of the Personality of Godhead, Sri Krsna, one can achieve the cessation of unlimited miserable conditions." (SB 3.7.14)

question: According to Maitreya, who both enjoy happiness, while persons between them suffer the material pangs?

options.B: The lowest of fools and he who is transcendental to all intelligence

explanation: "Both the lowest of fools and he who is transcendental to all intelligence enjoy happiness, whereas persons between them suffer the material pangs." (SB 3.7.17)

question: By serving what is one enabled to develop transcendental ecstasy in the service of the Personality of Godhead?

options.B: The common man through philanthropy
options.C: The feet of the spiritual master

explanation: "By serving the feet of the spiritual master, one is enabled to develop transcendental ecstasy in the service of the Personality of Godhead..." (SB 3.7.19)

question: Persons whose austerity is meager can hardly obtain the service of whom, who are progressing on the path back to the Vaikunthas?

options.B: The demigods

explanation: "Persons whose austerity is meager can hardly obtain the service of the pure devotees who are progressing on the path back to the kingdom of Godhead, the Vaikunthas." (SB 3.7.20)

question: The purusa incarnation lying on the Causal Ocean is called the original purusa; in His virat form He has how many legs and hands?

options.B: A thousand

explanation: "...and in His virat form, in whom all the planets and their inhabitants live, He has many thousands of legs and hands." (SB 3.7.22)

question: Vidura requested Maitreya to describe how which leader of all the demigods decided to establish the various Manus, the heads of the ages?

options.B: The Prajapati, Brahma

explanation: "...please describe how the leader of all the demigods, namely the Prajapati, Brahma, decided to establish the various Manus, the heads of the ages." (SB 3.7.25)

question: Which three incarnations of the material modes of nature did Vidura ask Maitreya to describe?

options.B: Brahma, Vishnu and Mahesvara

explanation: "Please also describe the incarnations of the material modes of nature -- Brahma, Visnu and Mahesvara..." (SB 3.7.28)

question: Vidura also inquired about the regulations for offering respects to the forefathers and the creation of which planet?

options.B: Pitrloka

explanation: "Please also describe the regulations for offering respects to the forefathers, the creation of the Pitrloka, the time schedule in the planets..." (SB 3.7.33)

question: Because the Personality of Godhead is the father of all religion, Vidura asked Maitreya to describe what?

options.A: How He can be completely satisfied
options.B: How He creates the demigods
options.D: How He sleeps in the water

explanation: "...kindly describe how He can be completely satisfied." (SB 3.7.35)

question: Vidura said that Maitreya's answers would grant immunity from all material miseries, and that such charity is greater than what?

options.B: All Vedic charities, sacrifices, penances, etc.

explanation: "Such charity is greater than all Vedic charities, sacrifices, penances, etc." (SB 3.7.41)

question: Being infused by Vidura, what did the chief of the sages begin to narrate?

options.A: The descriptive explanation of the Puranas
options.B: The four Vedas
options.D: The history of the Kuru dynasty

explanation: "...began to narrate the descriptive explanation of the Puranas, being so infused by Vidura." (SB 3.7.42)

question: The pure soul is in pure consciousness and never out of consciousness due to what? How then does he become engaged in nescience?

options.B: Situations

question: With the Lord as Supersoul in every heart, why do a living being's activities result in what?

options.B: Misery

question: Who "always enjoy happiness"?

options.B: Transcendentalists

question: By serving what is one enabled to develop transcendental ecstasy in service of the Personality of Godhead?

options.B: Children
options.C: The feet of the spiritual master

question: Vidura also inquired on which topic?

options.A: Regulations for offering respects to forefathers
options.B: Fruitive results of charity and penance
options.C: How the Supreme Lord be completely satisfied

subtopic: Ch 8: Manifestation of Brahma from Garbhodakasayi Visnu
question: Maitreya said that the royal dynasty of which king is worthy to serve the pure devotees, the family in which Vidura was born?

options.B: King Bharata

explanation: "The royal dynasty of King Puru is worthy to serve the pure devotees because all the descendants of that family are devoted to the Personality of Godhead." (SB 3.8.1)

subtopic: Ch 8: Manifestation of Brahma from Garbhodakasayi Visnu
question: The Bhagavata Purana was directly spoken to the great sages by whom?

options.B: The Personality of Godhead

explanation: "Let me now begin speaking on the Bhagavata Purana, which was directly spoken to the great sages by the Personality of Godhead..." (SB 3.8.2)

subtopic: Ch 8: Manifestation of Brahma from Garbhodakasayi Visnu
question: From whom did Sanat-kumara, chief of the boy-saints, inquire about the truths regarding Vasudeva?

options.B: Lord Sankarsana, who is seated at the bottom of the universe

explanation: "...Sanat-kumara, the chief of the boy-saints, accompanied by other great sages, inquired exactly like you about the truths regarding Vasudeva, the Supreme, from Lord Sankarsana, who is seated at the bottom of the universe." (SB 3.8.3)

subtopic: Ch 8: Manifestation of Brahma from Garbhodakasayi Visnu
question: Upon whom was Lord Sankarsana meditating, whom the learned esteem as Lord Vasudeva?

options.B: Lord Brahma

explanation: "At that time Lord Sankarsana was meditating upon His Supreme Lord, whom the learned esteem as Lord Vasudeva..." (SB 3.8.4)

subtopic: Ch 8: Manifestation of Brahma from Garbhodakasayi Visnu
question: After Sankarsana spoke Srimad-Bhagavatam to Sanat-kumara, Sanat-kumara explained it when inquired of by which muni?

options.B: Pulastya Muni

explanation: "Sanat-kumara also, in his turn, when inquired of by Sankhyayana Muni, explained Srimad-Bhagavatam as he had heard it from Sankarsana." (SB 3.8.7)

subtopic: Ch 8: Manifestation of Brahma from Garbhodakasayi Visnu
question: When the great sage Sankhyayana was describing the glories of the Lord, which two personalities heard him?

options.B: Parasara and Brhaspati

explanation: "...it so happened that my spiritual master, Parasara, and Brhaspati both heard him." (SB 3.8.8)

subtopic: Ch 8: Manifestation of Brahma from Garbhodakasayi Visnu
question: When the three worlds were submerged in water, Garbhodakasayi Visnu was lying alone on which bedstead?

options.B: A lotus flower

explanation: "...Garbhodakasayi Visnu was alone, lying on His bedstead, the great snake Ananta..." (SB 3.8.10)

subtopic: Ch 8: Manifestation of Brahma from Garbhodakasayi Visnu
question: For how long did the Lord lie down in His internal potency, appearing to sleep within the water?

options.B: One thousand celestial years
options.C: A thousand cycles of four yugas

explanation: "The Lord lay down for a thousand cycles of four yugas in His internal potency, and by His external energy He appeared to be sleeping within the water." (SB 3.8.12)

subtopic: Ch 8: Manifestation of Brahma from Garbhodakasayi Visnu
question: As the living entities came out for development of their fruitive activities, the Lord saw His transcendental body as what color?

options.B: Reddish

explanation: "...He saw His transcendental body as bluish." (SB 3.8.12)

subtopic: Ch 8: Manifestation of Brahma from Garbhodakasayi Visnu
question: The subtle form of creation, agitated by the mode of passion, pierced through which part of the Lord?

options.B: His abdomen

explanation: "The subtle subject matter of creation, on which the Lord's attention was fixed, was agitated by the material mode of passion, and thus the subtle form of creation pierced through His abdomen." (SB 3.8.13)

subtopic: Ch 8: Manifestation of Brahma from Garbhodakasayi Visnu
question: The sum total form of fruitive activity took the shape of what, generated from the Personality of Visnu?

options.A: The bud of a lotus flower
options.B: A great mountain

explanation: "Piercing through, this sum total form of the fruitive activity of the living entities took the shape of the bud of a lotus flower generated from the Personality of Visnu..." (SB 3.8.14)

subtopic: Ch 8: Manifestation of Brahma from Garbhodakasayi Visnu
question: Who was generated when the universal lotus flower was impregnated with all the modes of material nature?

options.B: The four Kumaras
options.C: The personality of Vedic wisdom, the self-born

explanation: "...the personality of Vedic wisdom, whom we call the self-born, was generated." (SB 3.8.15)

subtopic: Ch 8: Manifestation of Brahma from Garbhodakasayi Visnu
question: How did Brahma achieve four heads while moving his eyes in all directions?

options.B: In terms of the four directions

explanation: "He therefore circumambulated all of space, and while moving his eyes in all directions he achieved four heads in terms of the four directions." (SB 3.8.16)

subtopic: Ch 8: Manifestation of Brahma from Garbhodakasayi Visnu
question: Searching to trace the origin of the lotus, Brahma entered the water through what?

options.A: The channel of the stem of the lotus
options.B: The whorl of the lotus

explanation: "Lord Brahma, thus contemplating, entered the water through the channel of the stem of the lotus." (SB 3.8.19)

subtopic: Ch 8: Manifestation of Brahma from Garbhodakasayi Visnu
question: Unable to trace the root, Brahma came back to the top of the lotus and finally realized the Supreme Lord by what means?

options.A: By looking into the stem of the lotus
options.B: By wandering in space
options.C: By concentrating his mind on the Supreme Lord

explanation: "Thus, controlling all objectives, he concentrated his mind on the Supreme Lord." (SB 3.8.21)

subtopic: Ch 8: Manifestation of Brahma from Garbhodakasayi Visnu
question: At the end of how many years of Brahma's meditation could he see the Supreme within his own heart?

options.B: One hundred

explanation: "At the end of Brahma's one hundred years, when his meditation was complete, he developed the required knowledge, and as a result he could see in his heart the Supreme within himself..." (SB 3.8.22)

subtopic: Ch 8: Manifestation of Brahma from Garbhodakasayi Visnu
question: On whose body, like a lotuslike white bedstead, did Brahma see the Personality of Godhead lying alone on the water?

options.B: Sesa-naga

explanation: "Brahma could see that on the water there was a gigantic lotuslike white bedstead, the body of Sesa-naga, on which the Personality of Godhead was lying alone." (SB 3.8.23)

subtopic: Ch 8: Manifestation of Brahma from Garbhodakasayi Visnu
question: The gold on the summit of the coral mountain was mocked by what feature of the Lord?

options.B: The luster of His body

explanation: "There is gold on the summit of the mountain, but the Lord's helmet, bedecked with jewels, mocked it." (SB 3.8.24)

subtopic: Ch 8: Manifestation of Brahma from Garbhodakasayi Visnu
question: Brahma saw the Lord's chest decorated with which marking and a necklace of unlimited value?

options.B: The srivatsa marking

explanation: "His chest was decorated with the srivatsa marking and a necklace of unlimited value." (SB 3.8.28)

subtopic: Ch 8: Manifestation of Brahma from Garbhodakasayi Visnu
question: After being surcharged with the mode of passion and inclined to create, Brahma offered prayers after seeing how many causes of creation?

options.B: Five

explanation: "...after seeing the five causes of creation indicated by the Personality of Godhead, he began to offer his respectful prayers on the path of the creative mentality." (SB 3.8.33)

subtopic: Ch 8: Manifestation of Brahma from Garbhodakasayi Visnu
question: Sanat-Kumara accompanied by great sages inquired from ________ about truths regarding the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

options.B: Lord Sankarsana

subtopic: Ch 8: Manifestation of Brahma from Garbhodakasayi Visnu
question: Parasara and Brahaspati both heard the glories of Srimad-Bhagavatam from ________.

options.B: Lord Sankarsana

subtopic: Ch 8: Manifestation of Brahma from Garbhodakasayi Visnu
question: The Lord lay down for ______ thousand yuga cycles in His internal potency.

subtopic: Ch 8: Manifestation of Brahma from Garbhodakasayi Visnu
question: Brahma could realize the Supreme Lord_________.

options.A: By seeing into the eternal time
options.B: By looking into the stem of the lotus flower
options.C: By concentrating his mind on the Supreme Lord

subtopic: Ch 8: Manifestation of Brahma from Garbhodakasayi Visnu
question: At the end of ______ years, when his meditation on the Supreme Lord was complete, he could see the Supreme within his own heart.

subtopic: Ch 8: Manifestation of Brahma from Garbhodakasayi Visnu
question: The gold on the summit of the coral mountain was mocked by_________.

options.B: Luster of Lord's body

subtopic: Ch 8: Manifestation of Brahma from Garbhodakasayi Visnu
question: Thus Lord Brahma got surcharged with the mode of ________, became inclined to create.

options.B: Passion

subtopic: Ch 9: Brahma's Prayers for Creative Energy
question: After how long did Lord Brahma say he had come to know about the Lord?

options.B: Many, many years of penance

explanation: "O my Lord, today, after many, many years of penance, I have come to know about You." (SB 3.9.1)

subtopic: Ch 9: Brahma's Prayers for Creative Energy
question: Brahma said the Lord's form is eternally freed from material contamination and has advented to show mercy to the devotees as a manifestation of what?

options.B: Internal potency

explanation: "The form which I see is eternally freed from material contamination and has advented to show mercy to the devotees as a manifestation of internal potency." (SB 3.9.2)

subtopic: Ch 9: Brahma's Prayers for Creative Energy
question: Why does Brahma surrender unto the Lord, who is the cause of the cosmic manifestation?

options.A: Because the Lord is untouched by matter
options.B: Because the Lord rewards His devotees
options.C: Because the Lord controls the demigods

explanation: "I surrender unto You because whereas I am proud of my material body and senses, Your Lordship is the cause of the cosmic manifestation and yet You are untouched by matter." (SB 3.9.3)

subtopic: Ch 9: Brahma's Prayers for Creative Energy
question: According to Brahma, who neglect the Lord's personal form because of speculating on material topics?

options.A: Those who are destined to be dispatched to the path of hell
options.B: The pure devotees

explanation: "Those who are destined to be dispatched to the path of hell neglect Your personal form because of speculating on material topics." (SB 3.9.4)

subtopic: Ch 9: Brahma's Prayers for Creative Energy
question: Brahma considers the common people unfortunate because they are bereft of the all-auspicious performance of what?

options.B: Chanting and hearing about the Lord's transcendental activities

explanation: "...persons who are bereft of the all-auspicious performance of chanting and hearing about Your transcendental activities are certainly unfortunate and are also bereft of good sense." (SB 3.9.7)

subtopic: Ch 9: Brahma's Prayers for Creative Energy
question: Brahma takes pity on poor creatures who are overwhelmed by which urges, in addition to hunger, thirst and severe cold?

options.A: Strong sex urges and indefatigable anger
options.B: Greed and pride

explanation: "...and overwhelmed by strong sex urges and indefatigable anger. I take pity on them, and I am very much aggrieved for them." (SB 3.9.8)

subtopic: Ch 9: Brahma's Prayers for Creative Energy
question: According to Brahma, even great sages must rotate in this material world if they are against what?

options.B: Your transcendental topics

explanation: "Even great sages, if they are against Your transcendental topics, must rotate in this material world." (SB 3.9.10)

subtopic: Ch 9: Brahma's Prayers for Creative Energy
question: By what process do the Lord's devotees see Him, so that their hearts become cleansed and He takes His seat there?

options.A: Through the eyes by Deity worship
options.B: Through the ears by the process of bona fide hearing

explanation: "O my Lord, Your devotees can see You through the ears by the process of bona fide hearing, and thus their hearts become cleansed, and You take Your seat there." (SB 3.9.11)

subtopic: Ch 9: Brahma's Prayers for Creative Energy
question: Brahma said the Lord is not very much satisfied by the worship of whom, who are full of material hankerings?

options.B: The atheists

explanation: "My Lord, You are not very much satisfied by the worship of the demigods, who arrange for Your worship very pompously, with various paraphernalia, but who are full of material hankerings." (SB 3.9.12)

subtopic: Ch 9: Brahma's Prayers for Creative Energy
question: Brahma said the tree of planetary systems has grown by first penetrating the material nature in three trunks. Which three?

options.B: Brahma, Siva and the Almighty Lord
options.C: Vishnu, Siva and the goddess Kali

explanation: "This tree has grown by first penetrating the material nature in three trunks -- as me, Siva and You, the Almighty -- for creation, maintenance and dissolution..." (SB 3.9.16)

subtopic: Ch 9: Brahma's Prayers for Creative Energy
question: To whom does Brahma offer obeisances after stating that the foolish work of people will be cut to pieces?

options.A: Him who acts as eternal time
options.B: The Supersoul

explanation: "I therefore offer my obeisances unto Him who acts as eternal time." (SB 3.9.17)

subtopic: Ch 9: Brahma's Prayers for Creative Energy
question: Brahma said he is situated in an abode which will continue to exist for a time duration of how many parardhas?

options.B: Two

explanation: "Although I am situated in an abode which will continue to exist for a time duration of two parardhas..." (SB 3.9.18)

subtopic: Ch 9: Brahma's Prayers for Creative Energy
question: While the Lord enjoys the pleasure of sleeping on the bed of snakes in the water of devastation, what is stationed within His abdomen?

options.B: The four Vedas

explanation: "At that time, all the universal planets are stationed within Your abdomen." (SB 3.9.20)

subtopic: Ch 9: Brahma's Prayers for Creative Energy
question: Brahma prays to be empowered, as before, with what, declaring himself one of the surrendered souls dear to the Lord?

options.B: The power of annihilation

explanation: "May He be merciful towards me so that I, as before, may be empowered with the introspection to create..." (SB 3.9.22)

subtopic: Ch 9: Brahma's Prayers for Creative Energy
question: The Lord's activities are always enacted through His internal potency, known by what name?

options.B: Rama, or the goddess of fortune

explanation: "His activities are always enacted through His internal potency, Rama, or the goddess of fortune." (SB 3.9.23)

subtopic: Ch 9: Brahma's Prayers for Creative Energy
question: After Brahma prayed and became silent, the Lord understood Brahma was anxious about what?

options.A: The planning and construction of the different planetary systems
options.B: His own life span

explanation: "The Lord saw that Brahma was very anxious about the planning and construction of the different planetary systems and was depressed upon seeing the devastating water." (SB 3.9.27-28)

subtopic: Ch 9: Brahma's Prayers for Creative Energy
question: The Supreme Personality of Godhead told Brahma not to be depressed or anxious, because what he was begging had been done when?

options.A: It has already been granted before
options.B: It will be granted in the next millennium
options.C: It is granted at the time of annihilation
options.D: It is granted by the demigods

explanation: "What you are begging from Me has already been granted before." (SB 3.9.29)

subtopic: Ch 9: Brahma's Prayers for Creative Energy
question: The Lord told Brahma that he would see the Lord in all living entities and over the universe, just as fire is situated where?

options.B: In wood

explanation: "You will see Me in all living entities as well as all over the universe, just as fire is situated in wood." (SB 3.9.32)

subtopic: Ch 9: Brahma's Prayers for Creative Energy
question: The Lord assured Brahma that because his mind is always fixed on Him, which mode will never encroach upon him even while generating progeny?

options.B: The vicious mode of passion

explanation: "...even though you will be engaged in generating various progeny the vicious mode of passion will never encroach upon you." (SB 3.9.35)

subtopic: Ch 9: Brahma's Prayers for Creative Energy
